world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists (Haberland 1963 ms.) and SIL sociolinguistic survey (Kassell/MacKenzie/Potter 2017); no phonology of Tapei published

new_statements.quote: Stress was only marked on Wambrumas list, and even there, MacKenzie did not indicate stress on every word. As a result, only tentative conclusions about stress can be drawn. It appears that stress was generally on the ultimate syllable. If there is a suffix or it is a compound word, the last syllable of the stem is stressed and there may be secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tentative, from impressionistic stress marks on one 170-item survey wordlist: primary stress on the word-final syllable of the stem (i.e. final in unsuffixed words; stem-final when a suffix follows or in compounds). NOTE: the marked list is from Wambrumas, a Nanubae [afk, nanu1240] village, not from a Tapei village; the report covers Tapei but its Tapei lists carry no stress marks.
new_statements.secondary_stress: 'there may be secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme' in suffixed/compound words.
new_statements.exceptions: Suffixes and compounds shift primary stress to the last syllable of the stem rather than the absolute word-final syllable; authors stress the conclusion is tentative and that stress was not marked on every word.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited on the SIL standard wordlist (single-word utterances, recorded from one main informant per village). Word-level, impressionistic; no acoustic or phonological analysis. Applies first-hand only to the Wambrumas (Nanubae) list; Foley (2018) and Hoenigman (2015) treat Awim (Tapei) and Wambrumas/Imanmeri/Yamandim (Nanubae) as dialects of one 'Lower Arafundi' language, whereas Kassell et al. and ISO/Glottolog separate them (58% lexical similarity, RTT comprehension 56%).
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement found (Kassell, MacKenzie & Potter 2017: 17) rests on stress marks in the Wambrumas wordlist, and Wambrumas is a Nanubae village (ISO afk, Glottolog nanu1240), not a Tapei one; the same report's two Tapei lists (Awim village and Awim-speakers in Imboin) have no stress marked. The report covers all three Arafundi languages and treats their phone inventories jointly, and Foley (2018) and Hoenigman (2015: 46) classify Awim (Tapei) together with Wambrumas/Imanmeri/Yamandim (Nanubae) as one 'Lower Arafundi' language, so the statement is a same-language claim under their classification but a sister-language (nanu1240) claim under ISO/Glottolog. The quote is therefore a direct catalog candidate for nanu1240 (Nanubae) and only a proxy for tape1242. Foley's own 'Lower Arafundi' phonology (2018: 235-236) is explicitly from Auwim = Tapei.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison, Bonnie MacKenzie & Margaret Potter. 2017. Three Arafundi Languages: A Sociolinguistic Profile of Andai, Nanubae, and Tapei. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2017-003. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.quote: Stress was only marked on Wambrumas list, and even there, MacKenzie did not indicate stress on every word. As a result, only tentative conclusions about stress can be drawn. It appears that stress was generally on the ultimate syllable. If there is a suffix or it is a compound word, the last syllable of the stem is stressed and there may be secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3.2.2 'Stress' (p. 17): stress was marked only on the Wambrumas wordlist (a Nanubae [afk] village), and not on every word; tentatively stress is generally on the ultimate syllable; with a suffix or in a compound the last syllable of the stem is stressed, with possible secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme. The two Tapei lists (Awim, Imboin-Awim; Appendix D pp. 48-54) carry no stress marks, so nothing is said about Tapei stress specifically; sec. 2.3.2.1 treats the phone inventories of Nanubae, Tapei and Andai jointly as 'quite similar'.

sources.citation: Dye, T. Wayne. n.d. SIL survey vocabularies of Arafundi villages (Avambro, Wamblamas, Imboin, Kansomai), circulated in spreadsheet form via Paul Whitehouse / SIL; partly published in Davies, J. & B. Comrie. 1985. A linguistic survey of the Upper Yuat. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22 (PL A-63), 275-312 (Alfendio list pp. 283-311).
sources.note: Davies & Comrie 1985 (PL A-63, open at ANU) prints an Alfendio (Wamblamas = Nanubae) list and Upper Yuat survey notes that may comment on stress; not Tapei but the nearest published phonetic data with possible prosodic remarks.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1 (PL C-38), 731-763. (copy already held by the project)
sources.note: Lists the 'Arafundi stock-level family' (Alfendio 633, Meakambut 100?) in the population table and notes Laycock 1973 added the Arafundi Stock to the Ramu Super-Stock; only generic 'Sepik-Ramu phonology' remarks, no Arafundi-specific phonology or stress statement.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. Arafundi River; Tapei. NewGuineaWorld (Santa Fe Institute) web pages, Internet Archive copy of 2020-02-12 (live site now login-only).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Tapei page reproduces Foley (2017[2018]: 235-236) phoneme inventory for 'Lower Arafundi of Auwim village' (m n ɲ p t c k mb nd ɲɟ ŋg w ɾ j; i ɨ u e ə o a), pronouns and verb suffixes; family page lists all known data sources (Haberland 1966:62-64, Dye n.d., Davies & Comrie 1985, Kassell et al. 2017, Hoenigman 2015, Foley 2017:232-238); 'Historical phonology [under construction]'.

sources.citation: Hoenigman, Darja. 2015. 'The talk goes many ways': registers of language and modes of performance in Kanjimei, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/155259 (repository text bitstream read)
sources.note: Describes Awiakay (awia1234), a sister Arafundi language, not Tapei. Appendix grammar sketch sec. 1.1.3: each diphthong is one syllable and 'carries a single stress'; true vowel sequences are two syllables, 'the first one carrying the primary, the second one the secondary stress' (e.g. [wa-i] 'wind'). No general word-stress rule stated in the sketch; ch. 1 pp. 44-46 groups Awim (Tapei) with 'Lower Arafundi' (Wamblamas, Imanmeri, Yamindim). Nothing on Tapei stress.
